front: Section C — marks and assessment objective
back: 30 marks, AO2: design, make, evaluate and communicate. The largest section — aim for 8–10 pages.

front: Where does Section C evidence go?
back: Strategy, ideas, models and development in the informal sketchbook; the final detailed proposal in the formal presentation folio.

front: Two main design strategies in the legacy NEA
back: Sketching multiple designs and cardboard modelling, used side by side.
Getting stuck on one idea (or slight variations of it) instead of exploring genuinely different approaches.
Working with others through four stages: Discover, Define, Develop, Deliver.
Keeping the user at the centre throughout: Contexts, Requirements, Design solutions, Evaluate, Iteration.
Seeing the product as a system of parts (inputs, processes, outputs) and how changing one part affects the others.
Photograph every model from several angles, add the photos to the sketchbook or folio, annotate them and sketch over them to show changes.
At least 6–8 genuinely different concepts, annotated, with reasons why ideas are rejected.
At least two or three, each explaining what changed and why — based on testing, user feedback or a specification check.
Early, quick and rough — generation sketches, cardboard models, simple mock-ups and empathy modelling.
Later and refined — rendered drawings, block or foam models, CAD models and simulations, 3D printed parts.
Simulating the user's experience, e.g. wearing gloves to simulate reduced grip, and recording what you learn.

front: Social, moral, economic and environmental considerations
back: Who is included or excluded; ethical materials and supply chains; likely cost and scale of production; ecological footprint and the Six Rs.

front: What goes in the final detailed proposal?
back: Pictorial drawing, dimensioned working drawings, exploded diagram, materials list, finishes, manufacturing method, tools, specialist processes, CAD/CAM settings and justification against the specification.
Could someone else, such as a manufacturer, make your prototype from the information in your proposal?
Range of strategies, iterative process, broad and diverse ideas, factors applied, clear testing and refinement, a comprehensive final proposal and sophisticated communication.
